title: Burglars Steal M M Somaya's 1980 Moscow Olympic Gold Medal in Bengaluru
excerpt: Two unidentified men entered the former India captain's Indiranagar home on October 28 while the family was in Kodagu, taking four international medals, jewellery and cash; police have formed two special teams.
body:
• Burglars broke into former India hockey captain M M Somaya's Bengaluru home at about 2.34 a.m. on October 28 and stole four international medals, including his 1980 Moscow Olympic gold.
  • Also stolen were a 1982 Asian Games silver, bronze medals from the 1986 Asian Games and the 1982 Champions Trophy, jewellery, silver items and Rs 30,000 in cash; the total value of stolen property was estimated at Rs 3.53 lakh.
  • Somaya, 67, and his family were away in Kodagu; a neighbour noticed the front door open at about 7.15 a.m. and alerted him, and CCTV footage showed two unidentified men entering the house.
  • Indiranagar police have registered a case and formed two special teams; Somaya has written to Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar seeking efforts to retrieve the medal.

Burglars broke into the Bengaluru home of former India hockey captain M M Somaya in the early hours of October 28 and stole the gold medal he won with the Indian team at the 1980 Moscow Olympics, along with three other international medals and valuables, police said. The house, in HAL 3rd Stage, New Thippasandra, in Indiranagar, was empty at the time: Somaya, 67, had left Bengaluru with his family for his native Kodagu on the morning of October 25, according to reports citing the first information report (FIR).

The Moscow gold carries weight beyond its material value. India has not won an Olympic gold medal in men's hockey since the 1980 Games, according to a Hockey India report cited by Daily Jagran, and Somaya has written to Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar requesting that all possible efforts be made to retrieve the medal.

What was taken

The stolen medals span the peak years of Somaya's international career: the 1980 Moscow Olympic gold, a silver medal from the 1982 Asian Games in New Delhi, a bronze medal from the 1986 Asian Games in Seoul and a bronze medal from the 1982 Champions Trophy in Amsterdam, according to the FIR-based reports.

The burglars also took a 10-gram gold bangle, an eight-gram gold coin, two silver cups weighing 144 grams in total, six silver spoons, an 80-gram silver pot and Rs 30,000 in cash. The total value of the stolen property has been estimated at Rs 3.53 lakh. Somaya has stressed that the significance of the Olympic medal goes far beyond its monetary worth, Daily Jagran reported.

How the break-in came to light

The burglary came to light at about 7.15 a.m. on October 28, when a neighbour, Narayanan, noticed that the front door of the house had been left open and alerted Somaya. CCTV footage from the neighbour's house was then examined. According to the FIR, quoted by PTI, the footage showed two unidentified men entering the house at about 2.34 a.m. on October 28, one wearing a blue shirt and the other a red shirt.

"Subsequently, when the CCTV footage from the neighbour's house was examined, it was found that at around 2.34 am on October 28, two unidentified persons had entered the complainant's house."

— First information report, quoted by PTI

Who M M Somaya is

Maneyapanda Muthanna Somaya, a Kodagu native, played for India at three Olympic Games: Moscow in 1980, where the team won gold, Los Angeles in 1984, and Seoul in 1988, where he led the Indian squad, according to Daily Jagran. His career also included two World Cups, two Asian Games, two Asia Cups and three Champions Trophy tournaments, and he was conferred the Arjuna Award in 1985.

That record is why the theft reaches beyond one household's loss. The medal taken from the Indiranagar house is a surviving piece of India's last Olympic title in men's hockey, won 46 years ago.

Two police teams are tracing the suspects

Indiranagar police have registered a case under Sections 331(4) and 305 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, relating to house-breaking and theft. Two special teams have been formed to identify the suspects and recover the stolen property, and Vikram Amte, Deputy Commissioner of Police (East Division), confirmed the formation of the teams as the investigation continues, Daily Jagran reported.

"We have formed two special teams to trace the suspects. An investigation is on."

— Police officer, Bengaluru police

Police are examining CCTV footage and other evidence to identify those responsible, according to MyKhel's report. No arrests or recovery of the medals had been reported in the coverage published on November 4. For Somaya, the immediate question is whether the investigation can recover a medal that, by his own account to the chief minister, represents a piece of India's sporting history rather than a sum of Rs 3.53 lakh.

nri_angle: The stolen medal is from India's last Olympic gold in men's hockey, at Moscow in 1980, a piece of sporting history closely followed by hockey fans in India and the diaspora.
